steps.text: In a food processor, blend together basil leaves, nuts, garlic, and cheese. Pour in oil slowly while still mixing. Stir in salt and pepper.

importedNotes.text: This was incredibly good! I arranged boneless chicken breasts in a 9x13 dish. I coated each breast with the pesto and then layered sliced tomatos on top. Sprinkled on shredded mozzarella and baked. So good!
The proportion of ingredients were perfect! And its a relief to know that the more affordable walnut can be used instead of the rather expensive pine nut without casualty.
I absolutely love garlic, but next time I'll use 2-3. I used toasted pine nuts instead of walnuts. Expensive but worth it. I also added fresh parmesan and the juice of 1/2 a lemon.
I came out with around 2 cups of pesto. The recipe says 4 servings, but this pesto is extremely rich. On a smaller-sized bowl of pasta I use 2 spoonfuls of the sauce - not 1/2 cup.
The different nuts make whole different tastes, personally, I use walnut because they are so much cheaper. Roasting any nut first in a dry skillet makes the taste even better.
You can save it in fridge with a thin layer of olive oil poured over top - stays bright green.
If you're freezing it, a bit of lemon juice mixed in will help prevent browning.
I've reduced the oil from 1 cup to 3/4 cup to thicken the sauce, and I use only 2 cloves of garlic.
I wanted to make it a little less fattening. In place of the 1 cup of olive oil, I used 1/2 cup chicken broth and 1/2 cup olive oil.
I halved the amount of oil, and tripled the amount of cheese.
